title:
Effects of a CB1 Antagonist/Inverse Agonist (Rimonabant) on Functional
Recovery in Stroke Patients During Subacute Phase.
official: Effects of a CB1 Antagonist/Reverse Agonist (Rimonabant) on Functional Recovery in Stroke Patients During Subacute Phase.
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the effect of rimonabant in improving functional independence in post-stroke patients in subacute phase.

interventions.name: Same as the medicine tablets, but without the active ingredient

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age between 18 and 75 years.
2. Between 14 days and 3 months (14 – 90 days) since the stroke.
3. Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score between 2 and 4.
4. Barthel Index (BI) score ≤ 70 at screening.
5. Capacity to provide informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1. High suicide risk assessed by C-SSRS.
2. Known allergy to Rimonabant or any of the excipients used.
3. Participation in another clinical trial with pharmacological intervention the month prior to enrolment.
4. Any other condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, makes the subject's participation in the study inadvisable, such as severe heart failure or uncontrolled diabetes.
5. History of severe psychiatric disorders, major depression or prior suicide attempts.
6. Treatment with anticoagulants or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers (inhibitors such as ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, telithromycin, clarithromycin, or nefazodone, and inducers such as rifampicin, phenytoin, phenobarbital, carbamazepine, or St. John's Wort).
7. Patients with a history of ischemic or haemorrhagic stroke resulting in a residual mRS > 1, or with a pre-existing mRS > 1 due to other medical conditions.
8. Body Mass Index > 40 kg/m2.
9. Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
10. Fertile men or women who cannot guarantee the use of highly effective contraceptive methods, as defined by the European HMA-CTFG guidelines—i.e., those with a failure rate of less than 1 % per year when used consistently and correctly
11. Uncontrolled hypothyroidism, or a history of severe bone, liver, or kidney disease.
12. Inability to attend hospital visits.
